messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need to lock MVP for the Optimize toolkit. Customers and internal metrics pushed three asks: adaptive batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization recommendations, and eval-triggered alerts. Bandwidth is limited. I propose we prioritize batching+caching for public MVP and push alerts/quant recs to enterprise add-on unless customers force it. Thoughts?

chris: +1 on batching+caching as primary. Biggest infra lift is safe continuous batching (per-route policies + latency SLAs). Est ~3 dev sprints for a production-ready rollout (includes perf testing + fallback).

tess: For quant recs: we can produce a docs-first MVP (hand-curated profiles for top models) much faster than an automated advisor. Need telemetry for model exposure to be confident. 2 sprints for a baseline table.

ada: From CS: Enterprise X & Y explicitly asked for eval-triggered alerts tied to their prompt sets. They said it's a gating item for Dedicated. If we don't offer alerts, they delay commit.

maya: Tradeoffs: include alerts now -> pushes batching timeline. exclude alerts -> risk losing enterprise revenue. Which is riskier?

liam: Design view: full alerts UX is expensive. We can ship a webhook-first alerting MVP (no UI) that sends eval regression events and a minimal alert schema. That would unblock customers faster.

sam: SRE: continuous batching increases test matrix (seq lengths, model variants). We need a canary and an automatic fallback to non-batched variant if p99 latency spikes. That adds ~1 sprint of infra work unless we scope the canary small.

maya: Proposed MVP split:
- Public MVP (PLG): adaptive batching + prefix caching + simple rollout policy. Acceptance criteria: p50/p90 latency not worsen >10% vs baseline, cost/unit reduced by >=15% on internal small-signal workloads, canary fallback in place.
- Enterprise add-on (alpha): eval-triggered alerts (webhook contract) + quantization recommendations as curated profiles for top models.

chris: Fine if enterprise gets webhook-only alerts. I'll draft an API + webhook contract. We should also expose a flag per-tenant to opt into aggressive batching.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: infra-canary-test -> Tue 03:00 UTC (reminder) :gear:

maya: Action items: chris -> API & webhook spec by Thu; tess -> quant profile table for top 3 models by Fri; liam -> alert webhook payload example + minimal docs; ada -> confirm webhook-acceptance with Enterprise X/Y today.

chris: Example webhook payload I'll propose:```json
{
  "alert": "eval_regression",
  "model": "redwood-1",
  "metric": "concordance",
  "delta": -0.08,
  "run_id": "eval-2026-03-20"
}
```

tess: I'll run quant experiments (int8 / 4-bit-aware / q4_0) on redwood-1, redwood-2, and community-ggml top model. Will include latency/cost/quality deltas.

ada: Quick update: Enterprise X is okay with webhook-only alerts for alpha as long as we provide sample consumer code for them to hook into. Enterprise Y needs a short proof-of-concept. I'll coordinate.

maya: OK — if both confirm webhook-only, we aim for an alpha in 6 weeks. If either insists on full UI before alpha, alerts move to alpha+1 and we keep batching/caching as the main ship.

chris: One more thing — for caching we should scope to prefix/KV caching with TTL and route-awareness. No global LRU in MVP. That keeps complexity down.

liam: Agreed. I'll mock a minimal config UI and a CLI example for early customers.

sam: On canary: propose we gate batching by percentage and monitor: p99 latency, error rate, and cost-per-token. If any cross thresholds, auto-roll back. I'll add thresholds to the spec.

maya: Thanks — feels like a plan. I'll update the roadmap doc and flag enterprise gating conditions. Ping me when specs are up. :rocket:

ada: Will report back before EOD.

maya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
